segments.expected: Chapter 35 — Kiva: One Door Each Kellan was at the draft board at eight, in the black and gold, reading his own card with his hands in his pockets. Kiva saw him from across the boards and went over. She had meant to find him at the loft and had missed him; he had gone down the stair at six, Pru said, before anybody else was dressed, with his boots in his hand so as not to wake the room. Now he stood alone in front of the deal board with the green baize along its top, and there were nineteen cards on it, and he was reading the one with the Halden mark at its head as though it were a sum that would not come out.

segments.expected: "I'm pleased about the grey one." He went on down. "I'd thought being envied would feel like the top of the ladder. It feels like Gower eating a pasty and counting." He was quiet for three steps. "Give me the foot of the ladder, and you saying set." The Graving was full at a quarter to eleven, and the whole of it was green. Kiva had thought it was full a week ago, on the Saturday, against the Tarn's first four. She had been wrong. That Saturday there had been room on the tiers to put a hand down beside you. Now the green came down the steps to the floor's edge and stood there, ten deep on the bottom tier, and the boys who sold pasties had given up selling and were sitting on their baskets. The brown and buff of the Tarn sat in its knot in the middle. Meridian's colours were above it, all four of the first company, and Kellan among them in his black and gold.
